small_guidance:
- The current kernel recomputes conv for the full pool tile but only one (n, oc) per program — try larger BLOCK_H/BLOCK_W (e.g. 4×32, 8×32 with POOL=4 → CONV 16×128 / 32×128) and add num_warps=16 configs; also include num_stages=3/4 to overlap weight loads with the IC*KH*KW inner loop.
- Hoist weight loads out of the spatial loop: load `w_val` for all (kh,kw) of a given ic into registers once (KH*KW=9 scalars per ic), and reuse across the CONV_H×CONV_W tile — this cuts redundant `tl.load(w_ptr + ...)` calls inside the kh/kw static_range.
- Pre-pad the input by `KH-1`/`KW-1` (or rely on OH,OW divisible by POOL — they are, since 254/4 truncates to 63 outputs, but the boundary mask is cheap) and drop the per-element `(ih<IH)&(iw<IW)` mask in favor of a single tile-level boundary check; for interior tiles skip the mask entirely.
large_guidance:
- Switch to an im2col-style implicit GEMM: one program per (N, OC_tile, output-spatial tile) accumulating over a K dim of IC*KH*KW with `tl.dot`. With OC=64, IC*KH*KW=72, BLOCK_M=64 (OC) × BLOCK_N=128 (spatial) × BLOCK_K=72 single-pass gives a tensor-core MMA per tile instead of the current scalar FMA loop — this is where the headroom is on a 4090.
- Keep the pool fused as the epilogue: have each program emit a CONV tile sized `BLOCK_N = pool_tile * POOL²` along the spatial axis, reshape the post-activation accumulator to (BLOCK_M, pool_h, POOL, pool_w, POOL), reduce-max over the POOL axes, then store. Bias-add and tanh*scale stay on the accumulator before the max.
- Use channels-last (NHWC) for input/output so the GEMM-K (IC) dimension is contiguous; precompute the im2col gather offsets as `(kh*IW + kw)` deltas added to a base spatial pointer to keep address math out of the inner K loop.
